passages.quote:
1. Before you start

Before you can create a case using MyHMCTS, you or your organisation must have completed other steps:

Registered your organisation with MyHMCTS.

Set up your MyHMCTS user account.

The MyHMCTS registration guidance has further information and instructions. If your organisation has an account already, contact the administrator to arrange for your account creation.

If you need additional help with MyHMCTS email MyHMCTSsupport@justice.gov.uk. We aim to respond within 5 working days.

You cannot save a draft of the claim before it is submitted, so you should make sure you have all the information you need to issue the claim before you start.

2. Start a claim

1. Sign in to MyHMCTS using your email address and password.

2. Select ‘Create case’ from the header menu. Use the drop-down boxes to select:

Jurisdiction – Civil

Case type – Civil

Event – Create claim – unspecified

3. The next screen explains the eligibility criteria for using the service. For full guidance see practice direction 51ZB – the damages claims pilot. Select ‘Continue’.

4. Add references for the parties’ representatives if you have them.

5. Select the court at which you would like the case to be heard from the drop-down list.

It is important to enter the correct court. Where a claim must be started at a particular county court hearing centre under the civil procedure rules practice direction 2C, you should enter the code for that hearing centre.

6. You can give a brief explanation for your choice, if necessary.

7. Select whether you want the hearing to be held remotely.

3. Claimant’s details

1. Select what type of claimant is making the claim:

individual

company

organisation

sole trader

Depending on which you select, you will be asked further questions.

If the claimant is an individual, you must provide their name, address and date of birth. You can also provide their email address if you know it.

2. Select whether the claimant is a child – defined as someone aged under the age of 18 at the time the claim is issued.

If you select that they are a child, you will be asked questions about their litigation friend. If they are not a child, you will go next to a page about notifications.

Litigation friend

1. Enter the litigation friend’s first and last name, and their contact details, if you have them.

2. You must also upload the litigation friend’s certificate of suitability by selecting ‘Add new’ and browsing for the file. If you do not provide this information you cannot continue.

Notifications

1. You will be shown your registered email address and asked if you would like notifications relating to the claim sent to this email address. If you answer ‘No’, you will be able to enter an alternative email address. You must make sure you enter the email address correctly.

Claimant’s legal representative

1. Add your organisations claim reference, if appropriate. Your organisation name should already be pre-populated and should not need to be amended.

2. You can amend your firm’s postal correspondence address in case this differs from the address your firm’s account is registered with. Select ‘Yes’ and search for the address to do this.

Second claimant

1. If you want to add another claimant now, select ‘Yes’. You can then repeat all the steps in this section for the other claimant.

If you need to make changes to your claim after you have submitted it, send a request with the amendments to damagesclaims@justice.gov.uk.

4. Defendant’s details

1. Select what type of defendant you are making the claim against:

individual

company

organisation

sole trader

Depending on which you select, you will be asked further questions.

If the defendant is an individual, you must provide their name, address and date of birth. You can also provide their email address if you know it.

Defendant’s legal representative

1. Select if the defendant has a legal representative. If ‘No’, your next question will be about a second defendant.

2. Add the defendant legal representative’s reference if you know it and search for their organisation to add their address.

3. You can amend the defendant legal representative’s postal correspondence address in case this differs from the address their firm’s account is registered with. Select ‘Yes’ and search for the address to do this.

4. Enter the defendant legal representative’s email address.

Second defendant

1. If you want to add another defendant now, select ‘Yes’. You can then repeat all the steps in this section for the other defendant.

If you added a second claimant earlier in the claim, you cannot add a second defendant as the service only allows for:

1 claimant to 1 defendant

2 claimants to 1 defendant

1 claimant to 2 defendants

If you need to make changes to your claim after you have submitted it, send a request with the amendments to damagesclaims@justice.gov.uk.

5. About the claim

1. Select the type of claim you are making. If claiming damages for personal injuries, you should choose ‘Personal injury’ or ‘Clinical negligence’, as appropriate, even if there is also another claim – for breach of contract, for example. Otherwise, you should select the option that best describes the general nature of the claim.

Personal injury

1. If you are making a personal injury claim, select the type of claim you are making. Select the option that best describes the general nature of the claim.

Housing disrepair or damages and an ‘other’ remedy

1. If you are making a claim for housing disrepair or ‘damages and an ‘other’ remedy’, select if you want to add an ‘other’ remedy to the claim – for example, a declaration, injunction or rescission (cancellation). If you select ‘Yes’, enter the other remedy narrative.

2. Select if your claim includes any issues under the Human Rights Act.

Details of the claim
